7657.t: From μελῳδός (melōidós, “musical”) + -ία (-ía), from μέλος (mélos) "musical phrase" + ᾠδή (ōidḗ), contracted form of ἀοιδή (aoidḗ) "song".

7614.t: Unknown. Forssman doubts the authenticity of this word and Blanc supposes that the form was coined to explain εὐμαρής (eumărḗs).

7684.t: From μετέχω (metékhō, “to take part”) + -η (-ē, abstract noun suffix).

7617.t: Likely from Pre-Greek because of the presence of -αλλ- (-all-).

7609.t: Traditionally taken to be from an earlier *λέχ-σκα (*lékh-skā) with metathesis of the -σ- (-s-), a nominal formation from the same root as λέχομαι (lékhomai, “to recline”) and λέχος n (lékhos, “bed”).

7612.t: From Proto-Hellenic *lāros, from Proto-Indo-European *leh₂- (expressive root). Cognate with Latin lātrō, Latin lamentum, λάλος (lálos), λάσκω (láskō).

7616.t: Almost certainly a technical word of Pre-Greek origin, because of the many different variants.

7659.t: From the same Pre-Greek source of βαμβραδών (bămbrădṓn, kind of sprat) and βεβράδα (bebrắdā, kind of smelt).

7615.t: As for its accent, this word agrees with secondary adjectives like χρύσεος (khrúseos), λίθεος (lítheos), βόεος (bóeos), but conceptually it rather belongs to primary oxytones, like ἐτεός (eteós), κενεός (keneós), στερεός (stereós).

7601.t: From λυσι- (lusi-, “loosing, releasing”), from λύω (lúō) + -τελής (-telḗs), from τέλος (télos, “end, completion; here: dues”).
